In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evidence is insufficient for any of the cardiovascular imaging modalities to be used as a first-line diagnostic test to establish the presence or absence of heart failure, or to establish the presence of a specific aetiology.

echocardiography should be the imaging modality of choice in all patients with heart failure, and that the use of other imaging modalities (cardiac magnetic resonance and nuclear imaging) should be reserved to specific clinical scenarios and/or in patients in whom echocardiography has been inconclusive or has been performed but is not available for review.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no single test that is appropriate for every clinical scenario and that there are no absolute contraindications to any of the tests.
the literature search revealed a lack of evidence-based data to support the use of cardiovascular modalities in the majority of clinical scenarios.
the use of cardiovascular modalities is not limited to diagnosis of heart failure, but also includes the evaluation of aetiology of heart failure and the follow-up of heart failure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imaging should be considered in all heart failure patients, with echocardiography as the first line imaging test in most scenarios.
the use of imaging is essential in the diagnosis of patients presenting with heart failure.
imaging plays a central role in the diagnosis, aetiology, and prognosis of heart failure.
